summary: Security tightening: POST /user (create user) now uses a new OptionalAdmin middleware, so any request carrying credentials must be an admin with an elevated session (basic auth or recently elevated client token); unauthenticated requests still go through the registration rules.

statements.why: The change only narrows who can create users (router/router.go:158 OptionalAdmin, auth/authentication.go adminHandlers); it introduces no open address or data risk.

statements.text: Most of this change is in api/user.go (6 lines added, 17 removed).

statements.why: Doc text now says admins need an elevated session.

statements.text: The agent also changed api/user.go, auth/authentication.go and router/router.go, in ways plain can't describe yet.
statements.why: True but hides that these are login/permission changes, exactly what plain claims to read.

misses.what: Security fix on the create-user address: before, an admin's ordinary (non-elevated) client token could create users, including new admins; now creating users while logged in requires an admin with an elevated session (basic auth or /client:elevate).

Behaviour change: scripts/clients that created users with a plain admin client token now get 403; and a logged-in non-admin user can no longer create accounts through open registration while sending their credentials (only anonymous registration works).
